@Dasha Andriyenko @Emily Wachowiak

Did we ever make a final decision about where the panel should open if the selected text is no longer visible when the panel is invoked?

For example, the user could scroll down so that the selection is out of the viewport before accessing the right-click context menu. 

In such a scenario, the context menu would be the only way to invoke the panel, so my guess/suggestion would be that it should just be anchored to the location where the context menu was invoked by the user.

@Dasha Andriyenko @Emily Wachowiak 

Just a drive-by afterthought, sorry. 

In the `about:translations` page, we have a dimmed, localizable placeholder text here that says "Translation" to make it clear that this is where the pending translation would appear once a valid translation is triggered.

Did we consider doing the same thing here? I'm happy to leave it blank, but I just wanted to make sure the option was considered and recorded officially.
@Dasha Andriyenko here and below, I think the focus outline usually has a small offset (reference)

@Dasha Andriyenko 
(1) 
Name: "Checked: [on-screen string]" 
^^ I do not think we have a way to provide programmatic selected/checked state for <option> elements, but usually we just ensure the checkmark icon is communicated for a screen reader

(2-3)
the second "Role" may be a "note:" since it won't be announced as a link, but the <option> would function as such. But just in case, it's better to rename the 3rd attribute in both items so then the QA is not looking for a link announcement or engineers are not confused too ;)
This could be an <option> from the HTML <select> element so we don't need to customize anything.
@Erik Nordin could we include this button in the live region (that the textarea-readonly above would probably need to be wrapped into in order to communicate the changes to A11y API)?

@Dasha Andriyenko - the quick link button has to be either `<button tabindex="-1">` (with an accessible name from `aria-label` or `title`) or any `<div role="button">` container without any role and no `tabindex`?

Just in case for the engineers, and also for the QA to clarify the expectations (not focusable, but hovering with NVDA, for instance, would still announce the name and the role).

Name-wise, I think it would be beneficial to have `title` like "Translate selection" or just "Translate" - this would allow users with cognitive difficulties to hover over the icon button to see the visual tooltip with this name. Also, users with low vision would not need to try to distinguish the icon to know what this control would do.

As you said, there won't be any announcement for the screen reader, and we do not expect keyboard users to Tab to this button, but we still would need to ensure the button is programmatically the button so a mouse user of a screen reader like NVDA (someone with low vision, dyslexia, or cognitive difficulties, for instance) would be able to hover over this control and still hear the name and role (and click it, if they choose to).

[Added] This would be similar-ish to the "->" button we have in the awesomebar when a user types in something and the button is used to submit the search as an alternative to pressing Enter key

@Dasha Andriyenko: we could use `<mark>` in the Role section - it is a HTML tag that would provide all the needed info to an Accessibility API (the screen readers are usually not announcing it, but this is something that each user often can turn on, if they want to, plus, in the future, when the selection of text support is better, this would already be built-in)
@Dasha Andriyenko, The border of the panel would need to be `Text` (aka `CanvasText` in code, would appear white in the Dark Sky Win 11 HCM theme here)

@Dasha Andriyenko Do we need to specify the label for the gear menu or should that come from the reusable component? Just in case, I think something like  "Settings" would work great for it or "Manage translation settings", as it is called in the main Translation panel

@Dasha Andriyenko , just wondering if there can be a better choice for the background color for the translation field? As it is, it feels like an open text field. Might be confusing for users when they expect that this is an open text field but they can't edit it.

@Dasha Andriyenko , are we saying that in order for the user to select another piece of text, they have to click twice, once to remove the translation icon and one more to actually show their intent to move away from the selected text? I think we should combine this in one click. If the user clicks anywhere other than the previously selected text, both the icon and the previous text selection should go away.
thanks for switching to the info variant - that's actually more appropriate than the warning one here!

Having the "Change source language" button on the previous panel feels like an extra, unnecessary step to me. 

The "There was a problem translating" view has both an error message section as well as the language drop-downs. 

Do you think it would be a nice experience to make this one look just like the "There was a problem translating" menu, except the from-language selector is already on "Choose a language"?

From an engineering perspective, I'd like to push back on this slightly that we should choose one or the other. 

There would be a lot of extra logic and overhead involved to observe if the user clicked inside of selected web content or outside of it.

We have various behaviors it seems, as I'm trying this out myself. 
* When clicking away from the application menu, selections are deselected no matter where you click.
* When clicking away from the right-click context menu, selections are retained no matter where you click. 

My recommendation would be to have the panel behave the same way as the right-click context menu, which is to just leave the selection highlighted no matter where the user clicks away. 

I can't think of any UI components that try to be "smart" about it as described here. 

I don't personally see a great benefit to this nuance compared to what it would take to implement.

For the sake of discussion, have we determined that there is great user value in this behavior?

I wonder if this could be a 'Try again' when it fails so they don't have to hit done and re-do the flow. I'm thinking they could quickly reset their Internet connection then focus back on the browser window and hit "Try again". Unless that's not possible? :thinking_face:

Otherwise when they click on that full page option, will it possibly work for the full page translation because it's trying again, or will it throw the same error again if it's in fact an internet error that they haven't resolved? In that case maybe we don't even allow letting people hit this full page button if there's been a connection error, or in other words disable it?
